title: $B$-reasonability from a lower bound on atom probabilities
statement:
Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable on a finite sample space $\Omega$, whose law is a probability mass function $\pi$, and suppose $\mu > 0$ satisfies $\mu \le \pi(\omega)$ for every $\omega \in \Omega$. Then $X$ is $(1/\mu)$-reasonable, that is,
\[
\E[X^4] \le \frac{1}{\mu}\bigl(\E[X^2]\bigr)^2 .
\]
hypotheses_covered: law of X is a PMF π
μ is a lower bound on every atom probability π(ω)
replaced:
Let $X$ be a discrete random variable on a finite space whose law is a PMF $\pi$. If
$\mu > 0$ is a lower bound on every atom probability $\pi(\omega)$, then $X$ is
$(1/\mu)$-reasonable.
